bullets.title: August Core PCE prints dovish at 3.0% YoY; Fed hike pressure eases but spending remains hot
bullets.body: August core PCE came in at 0.247% MoM (3.0% YoY), below the 3.2%-3.3% consensus, driven largely by downward revisions in non-market services (36bp revision in prior months). However, real personal spending surged 0.55% MoM and Q3 real PCE is now tracking 3.2% — 75bps above prior estimates — with nominal core spending running at 10% MoM SAAR. Wolfe expects 2 more Fed hikes; MS says the softer print takes pressure off an October move but underlying spending pace is inconsistent with a return to target without productivity acceleration.

bullets.title: GDP revised sharply higher: Q2 to 2.2%, Q1 to 2.5%; income and savings rates revised up
bullets.body: BEA revisions lifted Q2 GDP from 1.5% to 2.2% and Q1 from 1.2% to 2.5%, driven by consumption, investment, and upward GDI revisions from asset income. Personal income was also revised cumulatively higher by 1%+, pushing savings rates meaningfully up across 2023–25. Morgan Stanley now tracks 3Q GDP at 2.4%; Goldman at 3.4%.

bullets.title: ADP September jobs beat at 90k vs 73k estimate; Friday NFP the key event
bullets.body: ADP September print came in at 90k vs 73k consensus — hiring accelerated for the first time since May — though wage growth was flat at 3.2%. JPM economists forecast Friday's NFP at 100k with 4.1% unemployment and 0.2% MoM wages; Hedgeye flags Friday payrolls as the critical near-term catalyst for rates direction.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 5.22-5.26%; biased lower near-term but 'higher for longer' intact
bullets.body: The 10-year yield sits at 5.22-5.26% with multiple strategists flagging it as range-bound to drifting lower (4.8-5.2% year-end target per 22V). Hedgeye notes UST 2yr dropped 9bps from cycle highs in 24 hours and bond market vol (PFIX) is signaling overbought. Treasury yields are on their 7th consecutive monthly rise — longest streak since 2011 — but dovish PCE revisions and Fed pushback on hike pricing create a near-term relief trade. 22V recommends TLT Oct 2nd 79/80 call spreads at ~$0.19 as a tactical bond-rally play.

bullets.title: S&P 500 at 7,717 (+0.6%); tech-driven rally with dangerously thin breadth
bullets.body: S&P 500 defended 7,500 support and rallied to 7,717, with JPM technicals targeting 7,922–8,052 if the uptrend holds above the 7,650 Sept 21 bull gap and 50-day MA. However, only 41% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 200-day MAs (lowest since May 2025) and equal-weight/Russell 2000 are approaching key support zones. The rally is almost entirely tech-driven; cyclicals (Materials breaking trend support, Financials/Consumer Disc approaching support), Energy stalling, and non-AI stocks down ~4% over the past month vs. AI stocks +6%.

bullets.title: Positioning extremely light; CTAs and HFs near historical lows in equity exposure
bullets.body: Hedge fund net leverage is at the 5th percentile with fundamental L/S ratios at historical lows. CTA equity exposure has fallen to its lowest since April — $75B already sold with a potential $75B buy program ahead. Hedgeye is pivoting materially net-longer, buying high-beta growth (IBIT, IGV, XLK, QTUM) on weakness with VIX below 17 supportive. JPM shifted to a Tactically Bullish stance. Citadel's Rubner flags today (Sept 30) as the seasonal low for mid-term election years.

bullets.title: Midterm elections increasingly in focus as a catalyst for the AI trade and policy landscape
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side firms (Morgan Stanley, JPM) are hosting webcasts on midterm election implications for AI policy, data center buildout, and infrastructure constraints. Morgan Stanley's panel with Ariana Salvatore, Stephen Byrd, and John Storey examines what changes post-November, including AI safety regulation, US-China sovereignty, and frontier model development. Trump signed a self-regulation pact with tech leaders and an EO adopting 'SI' (Super Intelligence) terminology, signaling a light-touch regulatory posture for now.

bullets.title: OpenAI DevDay: Dots agent and GPT-6.1 Sol launch; ARR surged 70% in Q3 to ~$70B
bullets.body: OpenAI launched Dots (cloud-based AI agent running across 4,000+ apps) and GPT-6.1 Sol at one-fifth Astra's token cost. OpenAI ARR surged 70% in Q3 to nearly $70B with B2B revenue doubling since July; a $500/month Pro tier was announced alongside a $30B funding round at a $1.4T valuation. Dots is restricted to paid tiers (Pro at $200/month+), signaling compute constraints. RBC views the launch as bullish for infrastructure names (NET, AKAM on agent traffic surge) and bearish for incumbent software (HUBS, CRM on disruption narrative); META rallied 3% during the event as Muse maintained App Store #1 with consumer AI ahead of Dots.

bullets.title: FTC opens investigation into frontier AI labs including Google and Meta; CIDs coming
bullets.body: The FTC launched an investigation into major frontier AI labs a few weeks ago, reportedly prior to the Hugging Face incident. Civil investigative demands for documents and key leader testimony are expected to go out in coming weeks, focused on alleged unfair or deceptive trade practices under the FTC Act.

bullets.title: Jefferies strategist Wood: AI capex cycle near peak; bearish on US bonds, bullish on gold
bullets.body: Jefferies strategist Chris Wood (hosting Oct 6-7 group lunches) has flagged AI capex cycle as close to peaking since early June. He is bearish on US bonds on fiscal concerns, bullish on gold, and sees China as a competitive threat to US equities. The SLM vs LLM architectural debate is a key discussion item.

bullets.title: Oil signals first lower-highs; WTI risk range compresses to $99.94; energy stalling
bullets.body: WTI and Brent crude both produced their first lower-highs in fractal/Risk Range signals, triggering trade-overbought readings for Hedgeye, which reduced its Brent position to minimum. WTI risk range compressed from $108 to $99.94. Gulf of Oman oil flows have rebounded to ~15Mb/d from a 5Mb/d trough but remain 36% below the pre-conflict 23.5Mb/d level. 22V notes oil has downside risk if Iran does not retaliate.

bullets.title: China stimulus judged too narrow to stabilize housing; 4.5% 2026 GDP forecast maintained
bullets.body: JPMorgan characterizes China's latest stimulus as execution-dependent and narrower than the Sept 2024 package: aggregate loan growth sits at a record-low 4.9% YoY, the 1ppt mortgage subsidy covers only ~31% of sales value (~CNY28bn annually, 0.2% of primary/secondary sales volume), and consumption impulse is weak as households save relief. JPM forecasts 3.6% Q3 growth, 5.3% Q4, and 4.5% full-year 2026 with momentum into 2027, but warns the initial boost fades without stronger fiscal follow-through. September NEV retail volume tracking -9% to -14% YoY.

bullets.title: US goods trade deficit hit a record $132.6bn in August; 3Q GDP tracking 2.4%
bullets.body: The US advance goods trade deficit widened to a record $132.6bn in August as imports rose broadly (led by industrial supplies and capital goods) while real exports gained only 1.4% MoM. Trade is a larger drag on 3Q GDP, but the impact is being offset by inventory contributions and consumption revisions. Morgan Stanley's 3Q GDP tracking estimate is 2.4%.

bullets.title: Defense: $1.5T budget push faces industrial base capacity constraints; AI vs China in focus
bullets.body: Multiple Hedgeye and Jefferies discussions highlight the Trump administration's push for a historic $1.5T defense budget, but note significant procurement and capacity constraints across the defense industrial base that limit realistic deployment of incremental funding. The Pentagon is prioritizing maintaining US technological edge in AI over China and Russia, while Europe accelerates its own defense spending with different priorities.

bullets.title: JPM technical chartbook: META only hyperscaler with bullish impulse; MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL lagging
bullets.body: JPM's technical analysis shows META as the sole hyperscaler with a confirmed bullish breakout from range. MSFT has stalled below August highs (support 477-486, critical 465-466); AMZN pulled back to 235-241 support after stalling near 283; GOOGL is trading sideways below 381 resistance above 290-306 critical support. SOX needs to clear 13,050 for a meaningful breakout. Yield curve flattening and momentum deceleration suggest a late-cycle environment; if cyclical weakness persists, tech rotation flows cannot be sustained.

bullets.title: Consumer spending resilient: real PCE +3.2% Q3, CC data mixed, wealth effect dominant
bullets.body: Q3 real PCE is tracking 3.2% (75bps above prior estimates). Citi credit card data for the week ending 9/26 shows Variety Stores ecommerce +9.8% YoY (decelerating from +12.4%) and Homegoods -1.3% YoY (a sharp drop from +5.8%). High-frequency indicators (Redbook, Fiserv SpendTrend) continue strengthening. Multiple strategists note that consumer resilience is wealth-effect-driven and would require a ~30% asset-price drawdown to stall; savings rate is 4.1% with historically revised upward trend.

bullets.title: TSLA Q3 deliveries estimated at 441k, -11% YoY; energy storage +30% YoY a partial offset
bullets.body: Multiple sources (MS Cyclicals, Hedgeye) peg TSLA Q3 deliveries at approximately 441k, down 11% YoY and 8% QoQ, driven by softer US demand and China domestic sales. Energy storage is expected to reach 16.3 GWh (+30% YoY). Energy business gross margin is guided below the historical 30%+ level (~26.5%) due to pricing pressure and tariff headwinds.

bullets.title: TLN announces CEO transition + $1.5B accelerated buyback funded by PJM capacity monetization
bullets.body: Talen Energy president Terry Nutt will succeed retiring CEO Mac McFarland effective Jan 1, 2027. TLN simultaneously announced a $1.5B accelerated share repurchase and upsized its total buyback program to $3B through 2028, funded by monetizing ~$1.5B in cleared PJM capacity revenues for 2027-2029 delivery years. FERC's 5-month suspension of PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement is slightly negative for TLN/CEG/VST but the long-term power price path remains intact.

bullets.title: PE secondaries market on pace to exceed 2025 record of $240bn; GP-led deals now majority
bullets.body: Global PE secondaries transaction volume hit $118bn in H1 2026 (+15% YoY, ahead of the prior H1 record of $103bn), putting the market on pace to exceed the 2025 annual record of $240bn. For the first time since 2021, GP-led volume (53%) exceeded LP-led volume (47%), with single-asset continuation vehicles representing 68% of GP-led activity. Average LP portfolio pricing was stable at 87% of NAV.

bullets.title: Mortgage applications -6% WoW as 30-year rates hit 7.30%, highest since Nov 2023
bullets.body: Mortgage applications fell 6% for the week of 9/25 as 30-year mortgage rates rose to 7.30% from 7.15%. Refinance applications represent 38% of total volume, purchase 62%. UBS flags this as a potential headwind to mortgage-dependent software revenue: ~20% for EFX and FICO, ~12% for TRU.
